origins: After divorce, abuse, a sexual past, repeated rejection, or being used, many people feel permanently marked. The phrase “damaged goods” may have been said to us, or we may say it ourselves. It treats us like an object that has lost value, and it can shape what we think we deserve in a relationship.
teaches: Scripture speaks of healing wounds and not discarding people. “He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.” The LORD says, “I will restore your health and heal your wounds… because they call you an outcast, Zion, for whom no one cares.” Isaiah 61:1 says He came “to bind up the brokenhearted.” “If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.” And “Because you are precious and honored in My sight, and because I love you.” People are not goods, and God does not mark down the wounded. The hurt is real, and it is not your identity.
self_statements: No one wants someone with my history.
I have less to offer than other people.
I do not deserve a good relationship.
errors: Feeling ashamed and concluding that I am defective.
Believing I am either whole or ruined.
Predicting that no one will love me.
questions: Where did the phrase “damaged goods” come from, and who first said it?
Is a person with a painful history a thing that has lost value?
What strengths have I developed because of what I survived?
What does God say about the wounded?
What would I say to a friend who called herself or himself this?
What kind of healing would help me most?
truth: I am not goods, and I am not ruined. I have been wounded, and God heals the brokenhearted. In Christ I am a new creation, precious and honored. I deserve respect and can pursue healing.
hw_truths: My history is not my identity.
log: Each day, write one sign of healing and one truth about your worth.
actions: Write who called you damaged and what you believe now.
Consider counseling, especially for abuse or trauma.
prayer: Father, You heal the brokenhearted and bind up wounds. Remove the label I have worn. Heal me, restore my worth, and help me see myself as You do. Amen.
hw_questions: Where did this label come from?
What would I tell a friend?
name_example: Sarah can write: “He heals the brokenhearted and binds up my wounds.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I'm damaged goods.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
